name: DACH cross-border company graph
demand: A proxy for the addressable data universe: Eurostat counts 3,185,294 German and 602,763 Austrian enterprises in 2023; Swiss statistics report 610,000 market-economy enterprises in 2021. The Swiss figure uses a different year and statistical scope, so these are not a clean combined TAM. They are records, not likely buyers. The reviewed sources do not establish search volume, installs, paying-user counts, or conversion to paid demand; those remain unverified. https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/statistics-explained/SEPDF/cache/39768.pdf https://www.swissstats.bfs.admin.ch/data/webviewer/appId/ch.admin.bfs.swissstat/article/issue230618442200-01/package
prices: Firmium lists unlimited free company profiles, Professional from €250/user/month, and Data API from €490/month; both paid plans have a 12-month minimum. Its page does not give a verified publication date. https://www.firmium.de/en/pricing/ GlobalEntity lists €19/user/month Starter, €59/user/month Enterprise with API, and €390/month Partner; its pricing page says it was last updated 18 September 2026. https://www.globalentityapi.com/pricing North Data lists API packages from €500/month and a €49/month Premium subscription. https://www.northdata.com/_data https://www.northdata.com/_premium OpenCorporates lists Essentials at £225/month for up to 500 API calls/month. https://opencorporates.com/pricing/ These are advertised prices, not verified sales or revenue.
copy_speed: The original kill-check missed a close, recent entrant: GlobalEntity says it launched on 24 August 2026 and added Germany on 26 August; its current documentation lists Germany, Austria, and Switzerland, plus ownership and monitoring features. https://www.globalentityapi.com/changelog https://www.globalentityapi.com/docs Global Database announced general availability of its Regis API on 24 July 2026 for company verification across government registries. https://www.globaldatabase.com/global-database-launches-its-company-verification-ai---regis Both dates fall within the requested window and make a generic normalized DACH registry API easy to copy or undercut.
platform_risk: High. Access and reuse differ by country and data type. Switzerland’s Federal Commercial Registry Office says Zefix is limited to individual searches and does not offer the full database or parts of it for download; API access must be requested. https://www.bj.admin.ch/de/handelsregister-zefix-und-regix Austria’s BMJ describes free high-value datasets but also lists a €90 one-time provision fee and €90/month for ongoing change data under its licensing information. https://www.bmj.gv.at/service/weiterverwendung-von-informationen.html Germany has a CC BY 4.0 bulk dataset through OffeneRegister, but the published dataset is a 2019 snapshot, not evidence of a daily official feed. https://offeneregister.de/ EU high-value dataset reuse still sits alongside personal-data and intellectual-property requirements. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/DE/TXT/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R0138
defensible_asset: A compiled-data moat is possible only if the product builds unusually reliable cross-border entity resolution, ownership links, and dated change history. The proposed asset is not exclusive today: Firmium advertises shareholder networks, monitoring, and daily synchronization; North Data advertises daily updates across many countries; GlobalEntity now lists the DACH countries and ownership/monitoring features. https://www.firmium.de/en/pricing/ https://www.northdata.com/_data https://www.globalentityapi.com/docs Switching costs could grow after a customer embeds the API, but neither that nor a proprietary-quality graph has been demonstrated for this lead.
build_effort: High for the stated breadth. The work includes source-rights mapping, country connectors, normalization, entity matching, ownership/event history, provenance, monitoring, and correction handling. Official access terms differ across the Swiss, Austrian, and German sources; AI agents can automate routine ingestion and checks but do not remove the need to resolve rights and data-quality exceptions. https://www.bj.admin.ch/de/handelsregister-zefix-und-regix https://www.bmj.gv.at/service/weiterverwendung-von-informationen.html https://offeneregister.de/ No reliable public evidence establishes a build duration or a solo operator’s actual maintenance burden.
channel: Use English- and German-language SEO pages, public API documentation and a self-serve sandbox, software/API marketplace listings, integration directories, contextual search ads, and opt-in partner listings. Keep acquisition inbound; do not use unsolicited email, SMS, DMs, or calls.
owner_hours_per_week: Unverified: there is no operating business or time log to assess. The ≤5 h/week limit is not demonstrated; the broad build phase is unlikely to fit it, and mature operations would still need oversight for rights, data errors, and incidents.
automation_reason: Estimated at 60% once stable: scheduled ingestion, schema mapping, diffing, routine monitoring, billing, documentation drafts, and first-line support can be automated. Human review remains for country-specific permissions, ambiguous entity matches, corrections, and serious customer issues. This is an estimate, not an observed operating result; official access and reuse conditions vary by country. https://www.bj.admin.ch/de/handelsregister-zefix-und-regix https://www.bmj.gv.at/service/weiterverwendung-von-informationen.html
moat_assessment: Weak in its current broad form. Compiled data meets the stated moat category in principle, but the underlying records are public or reusable and several incumbents already offer daily synchronization, ownership/network views, monitoring, or cross-border APIs. The defensible part would have to be a demonstrably better, maintained historical graph; the lead has not evidenced that advantage. https://www.firmium.de/en/pricing/ https://www.northdata.com/_data https://www.globalentityapi.com/docs
desk_test: One workday, no code or spend: choose a real cross-border company group and compare its German, Austrian, and Swiss records in the free Firmium tier and GlobalEntity’s public documentation/trial. Record source provenance, ownership links, event history, freshness, export/API limits, and price. Continue only if this reveals a repeatable buyer-critical gap neither provider covers; otherwise do not build the generic graph. This tests differentiation, not willingness to pay.
red_flags: The cheap kill-check’s competitor search was incomplete: GlobalEntity launched in August and now covers the same DACH geography, while Global Database released Regis in July. Firmium also offers free profiles and daily updates. Public price pages show offers, not verified customer payments; no verified revenue, churn, customer count, or underlying revenue event was found for this lead. The claim that only one competing launch appeared in the window should be treated as superseded by the dated launches above. https://www.globalentityapi.com/changelog https://www.globaldatabase.com/global-database-launches-its-company-verification-ai---regis https://www.firmium.de/en/pricing/
